in a large sample of Mexican patients with type 2 diabetes and controls, the PNPLA3 gene polymorphism (I148M, rs738409) was not associated with the presence or absence of premature coronary artery disease but it was associated with the severity of fatty liver and with insulin resistance in patients with diabetes and in the controls with coronary artery disease.

the I148 M/PNPLA 3 (rs738 409) polymorphism was associated only with the presence of premature CAD in T2DM, with fatty liver and increased ALT in pCAD patients, and with insulin resistance and subclinical atherosclerotic disease in controls.
the I148 M/PNPLA 3 (rs738 409) polymorphism was associated only with premature coronary artery diseases in patients with type 2 diabetes, but not with healthy controls.

the association between the I48M/PNPLa3 polymorphism and the development of pCAD in the Mexican population.
the potential use of PNPLA3 (I148M) as a marker for pCAD in Mexican T2DM patients, and as a marker of fatty liver, insulin resistance and subclinical atherosclerotic lesions in healthy individuals.
the potential use of this polymorphism as a marker for the presence of pCAC in T2DM and as a predictor for the development of CAC in the general population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PNPLA3 polymorphism is associated in a complex way with several metabolic and cardiovascular risk parameters and that this association is influenced by the presence of T2DM.
the association of the I148 M/PNPLA (rs738409 polymorphism with premature cardiovascular disease is not straightforward and it is influenced by the presence of diabetes.
the I148 M/PNPLA 3 (rs73840) polymorphism is not a susceptibility marker for pCAD, but could be a marker of subclinical atherosclerotic disease in Mexican individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PNPLA3 I148M polymorphism is a marker for pCAD in Mexican T2DM patients.
the PNPLA3 gene polymorphism is associated in Mexican population with pCAD in TDM patients, and with fatty liver, insulin resistance, and subclinical atherosclerotic changes in healthy controls.
